comment: The solar wind speed is currently elevated, increasing the likelihood of geomagnetic activity above background levels. A filament eruption on 8 August generated a CME. Analysis of available imagery suggests that the CME is likely to pass north of Earth; however, a glancing impact remains possible. We anticipate that the CME may arrive at Earth around midday (UT) on 11 August, increasing the likelihood of isolated ACTIVE to STORM G1 intervals towards the end of the first forecast period and the beginning of the second. We expect the enhancement in solar wind speed to be short-lived, and solar wind conditions to return to background levels by the end of the third forecast period.
role: independent advisory; score_effect=0 until prospective validation
